chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a thief (nabbash), so he delayed his punishment until Friday. When Friday came, he placed him under the feet of the people, and they continued to trample him with their feet until he died.

The resolution in these two narrations is to interpret them as meaning: when the action is repeated by them three times and the limits (hudud) are established against them, then killing becomes obligatory upon them, just as it is obligatory for the thief. The Imam is free to choose the method of killing as he wishes, according to what he deems most effective in the situation.

key_terms.نَبَّاش: Thief, specifically one who digs or steals from graves or buried items

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for executing a thief who commits theft multiple times, and what method did Imam Ali use?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam Ali’s (AS) execution of a grave robber (*nabbash*) by delaying it to Friday to maximize public deterrence through crowd trampling. The juristic resolution harmonizes the narrative by establishing that while execution is obligatory for repeated theft after established limits, the Imam retains discretion (*ikhtiyar*) in selecting the most effective method of execution based on the prevailing social context.
